h1: The 7 Best Ergonomic Keyboards Under $100 of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven ergonomic keyboards under $100, from split and wave designs to a keyboard and mouse combo, with clear budget picks.
summary: The Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is our best overall pick, a true split keyboard in the $25 to $50 bucket. The Logitech Wave Keys is the easiest to adapt to, the Arteck pair adds a wireless or backlit choice, and the ProtoArc EKM01 Plus bundles a mouse. Every pick here sits entirely within the $100 limit.
intro: A budget ergonomic keyboard fails in two predictable ways: the layout is only curved for show, or it is so different that you give up inside a week. Under $100 you can avoid both by choosing what kind of ergonomics you actually want before looking at prices.

We reviewed seven keyboards on paper, all in the $25 to $50 or $50 to $100 price buckets, comparing layout, wrist support, connection and extras. A budget RGB gaming keyboard in this data was left out because it is not an ergonomic design.

products.name: Perixx PERIBOARD-512B Wired Ergonomic Keyboard - Split Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.verdict: The cheapest genuine split layout with a padded wrist rest.
products.description:
The PERIBOARD-512B is a wired split keyboard with a fixed angle and an included padded wrist rest. It sits in the $25 to $50 bucket, well under the $100 limit.

It takes the top spot because a real split at that price is rare. The trade is a fixed angle and a cable, which the pricier wireless picks avoid.

Buy it for the lowest cost route to a split design. Skip it if you want wireless.
products.idealFor: Shoppers who want a split design for the least money.
products.skipIf: You want wireless or an adjustable angle.

products.name: Logitech Wave Keys Wireless Ergonomic Keyboard - Graphite
products.verdict: A one-piece wave with a cushioned palm rest and little learning curve.
products.description:
The Wave Keys has a one-piece wave-shaped frame with a cushioned attached palm rest, in the $50 to $100 bucket and well under $100.

Second place reflects that the wave is milder than a true split, which is also why it takes little time to get used to. It costs more than the Perixx.

Choose it if you want comfort without a long adjustment. Skip it if you want a split.
products.idealFor: Anyone switching from a flat keyboard.

products.name: Arteck Split Ergonomic Keyboard with Palm Rest, 2.4G USB Wireless
products.verdict: A real split with a cushioned rest and no cable.
products.description:
This Arteck is a split, angled keyboard with a built-in cushioned palm rest and a 2.4G USB wireless receiver, in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Third spot comes down to the fact that it is the cheapest wireless split here, though it costs more than the wired Perixx.

It suits buyers who want split ergonomics without a cable on the desk. Skip it if you prefer a wired board.
products.skipIf: You want a cable free of charging.

products.name: Arteck Split Ergonomic Keyboard with Palm Rest, USB Wired Backlit Keyboard
products.verdict: Split layout with backlit keys for dark rooms.
products.description:
This wired Arteck keeps the split, angled layout and the cushioned palm rest, and adds backlit keys, in the $50 to $100 bucket.

Fourth position follows from the fact that the cable and higher price outweigh the backlight for most users compared with the Perixx.

Choose it if you type at night. Skip it if you rarely work in the dark.
products.skipIf: You never work in low light.

products.name: ProtoArc EKM01 Plus Wireless Ergonomic Keyboard Mouse Combo, Gray Black
products.verdict: Keyboard and mouse together, still under $100.
products.description:
The EKM01 Plus bundles a wireless ergonomic keyboard with a matched mouse, in the $50 to $100 bucket and listed under $100 for both devices together.

Fifth place is explained by the fact that you pay for two devices, so the keyboard alone is less refined than the dedicated boards above.

Buy it if you want to replace both at once. Skip it if you already own a mouse.

products.name: X9 Wired Ergonomic Keyboard - Comfortable Typing, Ergonomic Full Size
products.verdict: A one-piece curved full-size keyboard at a very low tier.
products.description:
The X9 is a wired, full-size keyboard with a one-piece curved ergonomic frame, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Sixth place is down to the fact that a single curved piece offers less posture benefit than a split. It is a plain, low-cost way to start.

Choose it for a basic curved board. Skip it if you want a real split.

products.name: RECCAZR Ergonomic Keyboard, Wired Computer USB Keyboard with Wrist Rest
products.verdict: A curved wired keyboard with an attached wrist rest.
products.description:
The RECCAZR is a wired USB keyboard with a curved ergonomic layout and an attached wrist rest, in the $25 to $50 bucket.

Last place reflects that its curve is gentler than a split and the facts add little else. It is cheap and simple.

Buy it for a budget board with wrist support. Skip it if you want stronger ergonomics.
products.skipIf: You want a split or wireless design.

whatMatters.detail: A real split has two separate halves, while a curved board is a single bent piece. The split corrects wrist angle more but takes longer to learn. Look at the product images and the word split in the title.
A wrist rest reduces upward bend while you type. It matters at budget prices where it may be missing. Check the title for wrist rest or palm rest.
Wired boards avoid batteries but add a cable. A wireless board adds a receiver. Check the connection line in the bullets.
Aggressive layouts take days to adapt to. A gentle wave takes less. Consider how long you can tolerate slower typing.
A combo includes a mouse, so compare the single price with buying both separately. Check the price bucket and what ships in the box.

howToChoose.intro: Choose how different you want it to feel.

cards.label: Split
cards.text: Two halves keep your wrists straight. The Perixx PERIBOARD-512B and both Arteck models use it.

cards.label: Wave
cards.text: One piece with a gentle curve. The Logitech Wave Keys has this shape.

howToChoose.note: Most buyers should choose a wave unless they already feel wrist strain.

faq.q: Can I get a real split keyboard under $100?
faq.a: Yes. The Perixx PERIBOARD-512B and both Arteck models are split designs, all under $100.

faq.q: Will it take long to adjust?
faq.a: A split takes longer than a wave. The Logitech Wave Keys lists minimal adjustment.

faq.q: Is the Logitech Wave Keys worth it over the Perixx?
faq.a: If you want wireless and an easier transition, yes. If you want a true split for less, the Perixx wins.

faq.q: How do I set up the 2.4G model?
faq.a: Plug the USB receiver into a free port and switch the keyboard on.

faq.q: How do I clean a keyboard with a wrist rest?
faq.a: Wipe the rest with a slightly damp cloth and shake out crumbs from the keys.
The ProtoArc is listed under $100 for both devices, which can be cheaper than buying separately.

finalTake: The Perixx PERIBOARD-512B is the best ergonomic keyboard under $100 for anyone who wants a true split cheaply. The Logitech Wave Keys is the easier switch, and the Arteck boards add wireless or backlit choices. All seven picks sit within the $100 limit.
